title: Gruyère and Parmesan Mornay Sauce
summary: A smooth white sauce with nutty Gruyère and sharp Parmesan melted in off the heat, ready to pour or bake.

ingredients.item: Gruyère or Swiss cheese, finely grated
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the roux
steps.text: Melt the butter over medium-low heat, add the flour and whisk for about 1 min until smooth and no longer floury, without letting it brown.

steps.title: Whisk in the milk
steps.text: Pour in the milk slowly while whisking hard, so the sauce stays free of lumps.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring it to a bare simmer, turn the heat down and cook for 3-5 min, whisking often, until it is thick enough to coat a spoon.

steps.title: Melt in the cheese
steps.text: Turn off the heat and whisk in the Gruyère and Parmesan until melted and glossy. Avoid boiling it again, as the cheese can turn grainy.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Add the salt, white pepper and nutmeg. Spoon over cauliflower or other vegetables and bake until golden for a gratin, or serve warm in a bowl.

tips: Grate the cheese finely so it melts quickly and evenly.
Taste before adding the salt; Parmesan is already salty.
Emmental or a mild Swiss cheese can replace the Gruyère.
For a gratin, pour over cooked vegetables, scatter with a little more cheese and bake at 200 °C for 20-25 min.
storage: Cover the surface and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Warm over low heat, stirring and adding a splash of milk, without boiling. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
